title: Tipu Tree: Tipuanas You Can Visit
meta_description: One holds down a traffic circle, one stands in a bus terminal, one outside parliament. Five tipu trees mapped in Lisbon and Barcelona.
intro: None of the Lisbon tipus stands anywhere a gardener would have chosen. One holds down a traffic circle, where a crown 34 metres across had become the city's problem by 2018. One stands in the middle of a bus terminal. One occupies the triangle of grass outside parliament, which has kept a South American tree on its doorstep for about ninety years. The fourth grows in the garden named for the Portuguese defeat at La Lys in 1918. Tipuana tipu comes from the foothills of Bolivia and Argentina, a legume with feathery leaves and single winged pods that spin down like sycamore keys, and it puts up with pavement, drought and hard pruning better than most things. The Barcelona tree, about 101 years old, is the specimen the city measures its other tipus against, and there are plenty to measure: it is one of the commonest street trees in the city.
